description: ### Purpose
Performs a native Windows middle click at viewport coordinates or on a UI Automation element.
It presses and releases the middle mouse button, the wheel button, for actions such as opening links in new tabs or closing tabs in desktop applications.
Element alignment and pixel offsets provide precise control over the click location.
### Key Features and Functionality
| Feature              | Description                                                                                |
| Native Middle Click  | Sends a Windows middle-button press and release through the User32-compatible driver.      |
| Coordinate Targeting | Moves the pointer to absolute viewport coordinates before performing the middle click.     |
| Element Targeting    | Locates a UI Automation element and moves to its selected alignment point before clicking. |
| Position Adjustment  | Applies horizontal and vertical pixel offsets to an element alignment point.               |
### Usages in RPA
| Use Case                   | Description                                                                        |
| Open Links in New Tabs     | Opens links in new tabs of native or embedded browser windows with a middle click. |
| Close Application Tabs     | Closes a tab in a desktop application by middle-clicking its tab header.           |
| Coordinate-Only Interfaces | Middle-clicks a known screen location when no stable element locator is available. |
### Usages in Automation Testing
| Use Case                   | Description                                                                             |
| Middle Button Testing      | Verifies that a native element reacts correctly to a middle-button click.               |
| Alignment Testing          | Confirms that different element alignment points trigger the intended interaction area. |
| Desktop Regression Testing | Repeats native middle-click behavior after application changes.                         |

edge_cases: A coordinate outside the visible desktop may produce no visible interaction
A non-User32 driver returns an empty response without moving the pointer
Either X or Y being non-zero activates coordinate mode when no element is targeted
Zero values for both coordinates require an element target
annotations.expected_result: The system pointer moves to viewport coordinates (120, 240) and performs a native middle click at that position.
annotations.notes: Coordinate mode requires no element target and at least one non-zero coordinate. The parameter expression binds X and Y into the runtime parameter dictionary.

description: ### Middle-click at viewport coordinates
Moves the system pointer to coordinates (120, 240) measured from the viewport origin and performs a native middle click.
The `{{$ --X:120 --Y:240}}` expression binds the coordinate parameters before execution.

edge_cases: A missing element raises the driver element lookup error
A non-User32 driver returns an empty response without moving the pointer
Offsets can place the middle click outside the element bounds
The element target takes precedence when coordinate parameters are also present
annotations.expected_result: The pointer moves to the target element's top-left alignment point plus the configured offsets and performs a native middle click there.
annotations.notes: Element mode uses Xpath by default and applies Alignment before OffsetX and OffsetY. Element targeting takes precedence over coordinate parameters.

description: ### Middle-click an aligned element position
Locates the target tab item and moves the pointer to its top-left alignment point with horizontal and vertical offsets.
The native middle click then lands at the adjusted element position, for example to close the tab.
Alignment selects the reference point inside the target element before the middle click.
It matters when the interaction must occur near a specific edge, corner, or center position.
OffsetX and OffsetY adjust the final pointer location after alignment is applied.
parameters.name: Alignment

description: BottomCenter positions the pointer at the bottom edge and horizontal center of the element.
It helps target controls located along the lower middle boundary.
values.name: BottomCenter

description: BottomLeft positions the pointer at the lower-left corner of the element.
It helps target controls located near the lower-left boundary.
values.name: BottomLeft

description: BottomRight positions the pointer at the lower-right corner of the element.
It helps target controls located near the lower-right boundary.
values.name: BottomRight

description: MiddleCenter positions the pointer at the horizontal and vertical center of the element.
It provides the default location for standard middle-click interactions.
values.name: MiddleCenter

description: MiddleLeft positions the pointer at the left edge and vertical center of the element.
It helps target controls located along the middle-left boundary.
values.name: MiddleLeft

description: MiddleRight positions the pointer at the right edge and vertical center of the element.
It helps target controls located along the middle-right boundary.
values.name: MiddleRight

description: TopCenter positions the pointer at the top edge and horizontal center of the element.
It helps target controls located along the upper middle boundary.
values.name: TopCenter

description: TopLeft positions the pointer at the upper-left corner of the element.
It helps target controls located near the upper-left boundary.
values.name: TopLeft

description: TopRight positions the pointer at the upper-right corner of the element.
It helps target controls located near the upper-right boundary.
values.name: TopRight

description: OffsetX shifts the middle-click position horizontally from the selected alignment point.
Positive values move right and negative values move left.
It matters when the active area is not centered on the alignment point.
parameters.name: OffsetX

description: OffsetY shifts the middle-click position vertically from the selected alignment point.
Positive values move down and negative values move up.
It matters when the active area is above or below the alignment point.
parameters.name: OffsetY

description: X sets the horizontal viewport coordinate used when no element is targeted.
It is measured in pixels from the left edge of the viewport.
A non-zero X value activates coordinate mode when OnElement is absent.
parameters.name: X

description: Y sets the vertical viewport coordinate used when no element is targeted.
It is measured in pixels from the top edge of the viewport.
A non-zero Y value activates coordinate mode when OnElement is absent.
parameters.name: Y

description: Argument binds Alignment, OffsetX, OffsetY, X, and Y values into the runtime parameter dictionary.
It matters because the action reads positioning values from that dictionary before selecting its target mode.
properties.name: Argument

description: Locator selects the strategy used to resolve the native element named by OnElement.
Xpath is the supported default for UI Automation element targeting.
properties.name: Locator

description: OnElement identifies the UI Automation element that receives the middle click.
It matters because element mode applies alignment and offsets before sending the middle-button sequence.
properties.name: OnElement

summary: Performs a native Windows middle click at viewport coordinates or on a UI Automation element.
Supports precise element targeting with alignment and horizontal or vertical pixel offsets.
Opens links in new tabs, closes tabs, and triggers other middle-button interactions in desktop automation workflows.
